title: Deep learning and body composition model for predicting postoperative complications in colorectal cancer
summary: Body-composition CT segmentation and 3D ResNet-18 features are combined with clinical predictors; 154 retrospective CRC cases (99 development, 55 external validation), best combined AUC 0.944/0.855.
ai_technology: CT body-composition segmentation and 3D ResNet-18 image features are combined with clinical predictors to estimate postoperative complications in colorectal cancer.
organization: Department of General Surgery, The Third Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University (The First People’s Hospital of Hefei), China

evidence.tested: Body-composition CT segmentation and 3D ResNet-18 features are combined with clinical predictors; 154 retrospective CRC cases (99 development, 55 external validation), best combined AUC 0.944/0.855. Methods describe the segmentation, feature extraction and model comparison; Results report an independent two-center validation cohort and AUC. Prognostic association only; no treatment effect or patient-outcome improvement established.
evidence.unknown: limited to the stated retrospective/in-silico/prototype setting.
evidence.ai_role: CT body-composition segmentation and 3D ResNet-18 image features are combined with clinical predictors to estimate postoperative complications in colorectal cancer.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
